title: Invariant along an iterated orbit
statement: Let $I$ be a predicate on pairs of Boolean words, let $F$ map a Boolean word and a Boolean word to a Boolean word, and let $s_0$ assign a Boolean word to each Boolean word. Suppose $I(x,s_0(x))$ holds for every Boolean word $x$, and whenever $I(x,s)$ holds, so does $I(x,F(x,s))$. Then for every Boolean word $x$ and every natural number $i$, the predicate $I$ holds of $x$ and the result of iterating $s\mapsto F(x,s)$ exactly $i$ times starting at $s_0(x)$.
hypotheses_covered: I is a predicate on pairs of Boolean words
F maps pairs of Boolean words to Boolean words
s₀ maps Boolean words to Boolean words
I(x,s) implies I(x,F(x,s)) for every x and s
replaced:
Let $I$ be a binary predicate on Boolean words, let $F$ be a step function on Boolean
words indexed by an input word, and let $s_0$ assign an initial word to each input. If
$I(x, s_0(x))$ holds for every input $x$ and $I(x, s)$ implies $I(x, F(x, s))$, then
$I(x, F(x, \cdot)^{i}(s_0(x)))$ holds for every input $x$ and every iteration count $i$.
